$comment: One worked, validated example of every figure in the catalogue.
This exists because five of the seventeen kinds — compare, meters, cartogram,
nodegraph and timeline — are not used by any of the current 120 scripts. That
is not a bug in them: they need measurements or short labels that the copy as
written does not carry, and inventing numbers to make the spread look better
would be exactly the dishonesty the chart/diagram split exists to prevent.
So instead of leaving five components unreachable, every kind gets a block a
script can copy. Paste the `exhibit` object into a plan item's props, change
the data to the real figures, and the validator will hold you to the rest.
scripts/exhibits.test.mjs asserts every example here passes the same gate a
real script does, on the template named beside it — so these cannot rot into

dial.note: One ratio against its whole. `caption` may be empty when the template's headline already names it.

bars.note: One baseline, one scale. `emphasis` indexes the column the story is about.

exhibit.title: visitors who leave, by load time

meters.note: Horizontal, because these category names are sentences. Two to five rows.

exhibit.title: time to first paint, by cause

compare.note: Before against after, one measure at two times. One hue in two steps, so it cannot fail a colourblind check.

board.note: Three or four headline figures with no shared scale. Exactly one is emphasised.

cartogram.note: A tile grid, not a projection. Use the fixed region codes; an unnamed cell is drawn absent, never as zero. Codes: CAN UK NEU RUS USA SEU MEA CHN JPN MEX BRA WAF EAF IND SEA ARG ZAF AUS.

pipeline.note: Three to five stages. `bottleneck` is where the packet visibly waits.

trace.note: Three to seven rows. The counter counts the rows on screen and claims nothing beyond them.

checklist.note: Two to five steps. Mixed verdicts are the point — a list where every row passes is a list with ticks drawn on it.

nodegraph.note: Three to six satellites, SHORT labels only — a label grows outward from its node and must clear the panel edge. Past ~26 characters, choose another figure.

timeline.note: Two to four tracks, short names — the label sits in a fixed gutter beside its clips. `restAt` is where the playhead stops, 0–1.

radar.note: Two to four targets. They appear as the arm passes over them, which is what a scan is.

code.note: Two to eight lines; `highlight` indexes the one that carries the argument and is the only one that types.

browser.note: The template's native stage. Takes no data — the faults come from props.problems.

terminal.note: Native stage, for a joke whose setting is a machine. Beats become the shell output.

chat.note: Native stage, for a joke whose setting is a person.

sitemock.note: Native stage. LogoLadder and WorksOnMyMachine are built entirely around it and take no panel.
